subject: Meditech: Private deployment maintenance annex and staging compatibility check
messages:
From: Jared Klein <j.klein@meditech.io>

Cc: ops@meditech.io
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: upcoming maintenance and upgrade plan

Vanessa / Redwood team,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. We're planning a minor rolling upgrade of our private deployment (vpc-redwood-nyc-prod) to pick up the security patch for the inference runtime and the kernel set you recommended. Our goals: apply the runtime patch, validate model pin compatibility, and keep our existing pinned tenant versions in place unless you recommend otherwise.

Key constraints from our side:
- Maintenance window: prefer 10/7–10/9 02:00–06:00 UTC (narrow maintenance window)
- Business-critical traffic: daytime ET; any longer outage impacts care scheduling integrations
- Audit requirement: full preflight evidence (telemetry, canary report, audit log snapshot)

Can you provide a short annex describing: version pin semantics for private (what gets bumped vs what stays pinned), recommended canary cadence for a narrow window, and explicit rollback signal thresholds? I attached our internal runbook and the network diagram.

Appreciate a single-sheet decision summary we can attach to the change ticket.

--
Jared Klein
Head of Infrastructure Operations
Meditech Health Systems
j.klein@meditech.io
+1 415 555 0192

Attachments: meditech-maintenance-annex-v1.pdf, netplan_vpc_v2.png

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: upcoming maintenance and upgrade plan

Hi Jared — thanks for the clear constraints. Short answer: narrow window is doable with a tight canary, live KV cache preservation for pinned models, and a staged rollback ladder. I'm attaching a concise checklist and a suggested stagger plan.

Questions before we finalize the annex:
1) Are you able to open a brief 30-minute maintenance chat in the target window for live rollback coordination? (we prefer an IST/UTC overlap)
2) Are you keeping any customer-managed network ACL changes during the window (we need static NAT mappings for the bridge)
3) Anyone on your side required to sign the post-maintenance audit within 24 hours?

Proposed quick plan (high level):
- T0: canary node (1 node, 5% traffic) — run 20m synthetic + health checks
- T1: surge canaries (3 nodes, 20% traffic) — 15m observation, telemetry snapshot
- T2: staggered roll (30m slices) across racks — net quiesce pre-fetch, KV preservation
- Rollback triggers: increased 95th/99th latency beyond 2x baseline, error-rate spike >1% sustained for 5m, KB mismatch/invalid cache warming on canary

I'll draft the one-sheet and the annex for your change ticket and share a Drive link. CCing Karthik and Rishi to flesh out the rollback mechanics and network gating.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Reliability (Redwood Inference)
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Attachment: preflight-checklist.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Jared Klein <j.klein@meditech.io>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: upcoming maintenance and upgrade plan

Vanessa / Jared — adding technical detail on the rollback mechanics and pin handling.

Summary (technical):
- Version pinning semantics: customer pin = model binary + runtime-compat marker. We will push a runtime patch that is ABI-compatible for all pinned model binaries we ship; pinned model hashes are immutable unless you elect unpin. That means: if we detect a mismatch in runtime->model ABI (very unlikely for this patch), we will automatically fail canary and not proceed.

- KV cache & prefix handling: we will preserve key namespaces for pinned tenants. During node-level restart we snapshot the active KV checkpoint and rehydrate on replacement nodes before traffic ramp. If hydration fails we will mark the node as non-ready and exclude from LB.

- Canary cadence (narrow window tuning):
  * 02:00 UTC - start canary node (warm 10m) + synthetic load (replicate 500 small requests/min)
  * 02:20 UTC - run functional evals (prompt set) and compare token-level latencies
  * 02:40 UTC - expand to 3 canary nodes (20% traffic) for 20m
  * 03:05 UTC - if metrics OK, stage 1 roll (25% of racks)

- Rollback ladder: 
  1) Abort and remain on old runtime (canary failed)
  2) If partial rollout fails, auto-evict evicted nodes and revert route-level weights to prior set (traffic steering)
  3) If network ACL mismatch detected (reachability failed) — engage NetOps to restore static mappings and rehydrate caches

Signals we'll surface in the ops chat: canary health, 95/99 latency deltas, jitter, error rate per route, KV hydration status, live audit log snapshot link.

I'll prepare a terse runbook snippet you can drop into the change ticket.

—Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Klein <j.klein@meditech.io>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: upcoming maintenance and upgrade plan

Quick operational notes — flagged items and mitigations: 
- Timebox enforcement: because your window is narrow we'll compress canary checks and rely on synthetic/eval-driven checks rather than long-sticky real traffic. That increases risk of surface regressions; we'll surface this in the one-sheet.
- Network gating: please confirm whether your edge firewall allows ephemeral source ranges from our patch orchestrator (we will supply the CIDR list). If not, we need a manual NAT route for bridge traffic.
- Post-maintenance telemetry: we will snapshot the token-level cost and latency logs at T0 and Tn+2h — please confirm retention for the snapshot for audit.

Suggested acceptance criteria (for your change board):
1) Canary green for 30m cumulative (synthetic+small fraction of live)
2) No KV hydration errors across canaries
3) No route-level error rate >1% for 15m

If all good, we will publish the one-sheet and I will be on the 02:00 UTC chat to coordinate script-driven rollbacks.

—Rishi
Principal Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
